# 2 Kings Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 239r–240v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_018_page_476.jpg, 2KI_018_page_477.jpg, 2KI_018_page_478.jpg, 2KI_018_page_479.jpg

---

**18:1** And-it-was in-the-third year of-Hoshea son of-Elah king of-Yisra'el, became-king [malakh] Chizkiyahu son of-Achaz king of-Yehudah.

**18:2** A-son of-twenty-five years [ben esrim ve-chamesh shanah] he-was when-he-became-king, and-twenty-nine years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Avi daughter of-Zekharyah.

**18:3** And-he-did the-right [ha-yashar] in-the-eyes of-YHWH, according-to-all that David his-father had-done.

**18:4** He removed [hesir] the-high-places [ha-bamot], and-shattered [vayeshabber] the-pillars [ha-matstsevot], and-cut-down [vayikhrot] the-Asherah [ha-asherah], and-crushed [vayikhot] the-bronze serpent [nechash ha-nechoshet] that Mosheh had-made, for until those days the-sons of-Yisra'el were-burning-incense [meqatterim] to-it, and-he-called-it [vayiqra lo] Nechushtan.

**18:5** In-YHWH God of-Yisra'el he-trusted [batach], and-after-him there-was-none [lo hayah] like-him among-all the-kings of-Yehudah, nor-among-those who-were before-him.

**18:6** And-he-clung [vayidbaq] to-YHWH; he-did-not turn-aside [lo sar] from-after-him, and-he-kept [vayishmor] his-commandments [mitsvotav] that YHWH had-commanded Mosheh.

**18:7** And-YHWH was with-him ['immo]; in-all that he-went-out [yetse] he-prospered [yaskil]. And-he-rebelled [vayimrod] against-the-king of-Ashur and-did-not serve-him ['avado].

**18:8** He struck [hikkah] the-Pelishtim to-Azzah and-its-borders [gevuleha], from-tower of-watchmen [migdal notsrim] to-fortified city [ir mibtsar].

**18:9** And-it-was in-the-fourth year of-the-king Chizkiyahu — it [was] the-seventh year of-Hoshea son of-Elah king of-Yisra'el — came-up [alah] Shalmaneser king of-Ashur against Shomron and-besieged [vayatsar] upon-it.

**18:10** And-they-captured-it [vayilkeduha] at-the-end of-three years; in-the-sixth year of-Chizkiyahu — it [was] the-ninth year of-Hoshea king of-Yisra'el — Shomron was-captured [nilkedah].

**18:11** And-exiled [vayegel] the-king of-Ashur Yisra'el to-Ashur, and-settled-them [vayanchum] in-Chalach and-in-Chavor [by] the-river Gozan and-[in] the-cities of-Maday,

**18:12** because [asher] they-did-not listen [lo sham'u] to-the-voice of-YHWH their-God, and-transgressed [vaya'avru] his-covenant [berito], all that Mosheh servant of-YHWH had-commanded. And-they-did-not listen [lo sham'u] and-did-not do [lo asu].

**18:13** And-in-the-fourteenth year of-the-king Chizkiyahu, came-up [alah] Sancheriv king of-Ashur against all the-fortified cities [arey ha-mibtsar] of-Yehudah and-seized-them [vayitpesum].

**18:14** And-sent Chizkiyahu king of-Yehudah to the-king of-Ashur to-Lakhish, saying: I-have-sinned [chatati]; turn [shuv] from-upon-me. Whatever you-put [titten] upon-me I-will-bear [essa]. And-imposed [vayasem] the-king of-Ashur upon Chizkiyahu king of-Yehudah three-hundred talents [kikkar] of-silver and-thirty talents of-gold.

**18:15** And-gave [vayitten] Chizkiyahu all the-silver that-was-found in-the-house of-YHWH and-in-the-treasuries [otsrot] of-the-house of-the-king.

**18:16** At-that time Chizkiyahu cut-off [qitsa'] the-doors [daltot] of-the-temple [heykhal] of-YHWH and-the-doorposts ['omanot] that Chizkiyahu king of-Yehudah had-overlaid [tsippah], and-gave-them [vayittenem] to-the-king of-Ashur.

**18:17** And-sent the-king of-Ashur the-Tartan and-the-Rav-Saris and-the-Rav-Shakeh from-Lakhish to the-king Chizkiyahu with-a-heavy force [be-chel kaved] to-Yerushalayim. And-they-went-up and-came to-Yerushalayim, and-they-went-up and-came and-stood by-the-conduit [te'alat] of-the-upper pool [ha-berekhah ha-elyonah], which [is] on-the-highway [mesillat] of-the-field of-the-washer [sedeh khovesh].

**18:18** And-they-called to the-king, and-went-out to-them Elyaqim son of-Chilqiyahu who [was] over the-house [al ha-bayit], and-Shevnah the-scribe [ha-sofer], and-Yo'ach son of-Asaph the-recorder [ha-mazkir].

**18:19** And-said to-them the-Rav-Shakeh: Say, please, to Chizkiyahu: Thus says the-great king [ha-melekh ha-gadol], the-king of-Ashur: What [is] this trust [ha-bittachon] that you-have-trusted [batachta]?

**18:20** You-say — only [akh] a-word of-lips [devar sefatayim] — [there is] counsel ['etsah] and-strength [gevurah] for-the-war. Now, upon-whom have-you-trusted [batachta] that you-have-rebelled [maradta] against-me?

**18:21** Now, behold, you-trust [batachta] upon the-staff [mish'enet] of-this crushed [ha-ratuts] reed [ha-qaneh], upon Mitsrayim, which if-a-man leans [yissamekh] upon-it, it-goes into-his-palm [kappo] and-pierces-it [neqavah]. So [is] Par'oh king of-Mitsrayim to-all who-trust upon-him.

**18:22** And-if you-say to-me: In-YHWH our-God we-trust [batachnu] — is-he-not the-one whose high-places [bamotav] and-whose altars [mizbehotav] Chizkiyahu has-removed [hesir], and-has-said to-Yehudah and-to-Yerushalayim: Before this altar you-shall-bow-down in-Yerushalayim?

**18:23** And-now, wager [hit'arev], please, with my-master the-king of-Ashur, and-I-will-give to-you two-thousand horses [susim] — if you-are-able [tukhal] to-set [latet] upon-them riders [rokhevim].

**18:24** And-how will-you-turn-back [tashiv] the-face of-one captain [pachah] of-the-least [ha-qetannim] of-my-master's servants ['avdey adoni]? And-you-trust upon Mitsrayim for-chariots [le-rekhev] and-for-horsemen [u-le-farashim]?

**18:25** Now, without [ha-mibbal'adey] YHWH have-I-come-up against this place [ha-maqom ha-zeh] to-destroy-it [le-hashchitah]? YHWH said to-me: Go-up [aleh] against this land [ha-arets ha-zo't] and-destroy-it [ve-hashchitah].

**18:26** And-said Elyaqim son of-Chilqiyahu and-Shevnah and-Yo'ach to the-Rav-Shakeh: Speak, please, to-your-servants [in] Aramit [Aramaic], for we-hear [shom'im] [it], and-do-not speak with-us [in] Yehudit [Judahite/Hebrew] in-the-ears of-the-people who [are] on the-wall.

**18:27** And-said to-them the-Rav-Shakeh: Is-it to-your-master and-to-you [that] my-master has-sent-me to-speak these words [ha-devarim ha-elleh]? Is-it-not to the-men [ha-anashim] who-sit [ha-yoshevim] on the-wall, to-eat their-dung [chareyhem] and-to-drink the-water of-their-feet [mey ragleihem] with-you?

**18:28** And-stood the-Rav-Shakeh and-called with-a-great voice [qol gadol] in-Yehudit and-spoke and-said: Hear [shim'u] the-word of-the-great king, the-king of-Ashur!

**18:29** Thus says the-king: Let-not Chizkiyahu deceive-you [yashi' etkhem], for he-is-not-able [lo yukhal] to-deliver-you [le-hatstsil etkhem] from-his-hand.

**18:30** And-let-not Chizkiyahu make-you-trust [yavtiach] to-YHWH, saying: YHWH will-surely-deliver-us [hatssel yatssilenu], and-this city will-not be-given [lo tinnathen] into-the-hand of-the-king of-Ashur.

**18:31** Do-not listen [al tishme'u] to Chizkiyahu, for thus says the-king of-Ashur: Make [asu] with-me a-blessing [berakhah] and-come-out [tse'u] to-me, and-eat [ikhlu], each-man his-vine [gafno] and-each-man his-fig-tree [te'enato], and-drink [shetu] each-man the-waters of-his-cistern [boro],

**18:32** until I-come and-take-you [ve-laqachti etkhem] to a-land like-your-land ['erets ke-artsekhem], a-land of-grain [dagan] and-new-wine [tirosh], a-land of-bread [lechem] and-vineyards [keramim], a-land of-olive-trees [zeytim] and-honey [devash]. And-live and-do-not die [ve-chiyu ve-al tamutu]. And-do-not listen to Chizkiyahu, for he-misleads-you [yasit etkhem], saying: YHWH will-deliver-us [yatssilenu].

**18:33** Have the-gods of-the-nations delivered [hitstsilu], each his-land, from-the-hand of-the-king of-Ashur?

**18:34** Where [are] the-gods of-Chamat and-Arpad? Where [are] the-gods of-Sepharvaim, Hena and-Ivvah? Did-they-deliver [hittsilu] Shomron from-my-hand?

**18:35** Who among-all the-gods of-the-lands ['aratsot] has-delivered [hittsilu] their-land from-my-hand, that YHWH should-deliver [yatsil] Yerushalayim from-my-hand?

**18:36** And-the-people were-silent [vayachashu ha-am] and-did-not answer [lo anu] him a-word [davar], for the-command [mitsvat] of-the-king [was], saying: Do-not answer-him [lo ta'anuhu].

**18:37** And-came Elyaqim son of-Chilqiyahu who [was] over the-house, and-Shevnah the-scribe, and-Yo'ach son of-Asaph the-recorder, to Chizkiyahu with-torn garments [qeru'ey begadim], and-told-him the-words of-the-Rav-Shakeh.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — Nechushtan:** Hezekiah destroys the bronze serpent Moses made in Numbers 21:8-9. The name *Nechushtan* is a wordplay: *nachash* (serpent) + *nechoshet* (bronze) + a contemptuous diminutive ending. By naming it, Hezekiah demythologizes it — reducing a sacred relic to a thing with a mocking name. This is the most radical reform in Judah's history to this point.

**v.5 — "after him there was none like him":** This superlative is striking because 23:25 says the same of Josiah. The narrator gives the same highest praise to both — creating a deliberate tension that scholars have long debated. Hezekiah is "like none" in trust (*bitachon*); Josiah is "like none" in Torah-obedience.

**v.17 — Rabshakeh at the upper pool:** The location is the same place where Isaiah met Ahaz in Isaiah 7:3. The narrator connects the scenes: where Ahaz failed to trust YHWH, his son Hezekiah will be tested in the same place by the same enemy (Assyria).

**v.22 — Rabshakeh's theological argument:** The Rabshakeh's most devastating point: Hezekiah destroyed the high places and altars — so how can he now claim YHWH's protection? The argument assumes that removing cult sites angers the deity. It is a pagan misunderstanding of centralized worship, but it would have been persuasive to the people on the wall.

**v.26 — *Yehudit* and *Aramit*:** The officials ask the Rabshakeh to speak Aramaic (the diplomatic language) rather than Hebrew (the people's language). His refusal to switch — and his deliberate escalation to shouting — shows this is not diplomacy but psychological warfare. The speech targets the people, not the leaders.

**v.27 — *chareyhem* and *mey ragleihem*:** Crude siege-warfare language. The Rabshakeh describes the fate of the besieged in vulgar terms to terrify the listeners on the wall: they will be reduced to eating and drinking their own waste.

*— EMET*
